subject: Re: Novio Health — subprocessor residency and evidence for procurement
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@noviohealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@noviohealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Novio procurement — subprocessor residency & CAIQ follow-up

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As we start procurement and the vendor assessment, our security team asked for a few specific artifacts so we can complete the legal/IT review: 

- Full subprocessor roster (name, service provided, data residency for production, and whether they have CAIQ/SOC2 evidence).
- Any onshore (US-only) hosting options and whether KMS keys can be restricted to a customer-managed flow.
- A short summary (1 page) of how you handle transient/ephemeral keys and third-party access during inference (we want to confirm minimal transitive access).

We have attached Novio's standard SIG-lite for vendors — if you can return a completed SIG-lite or at minimum the responses for the subprocessor/dataflow sections that would speed things up. Procurement is hoping to get the packet back by EOD next Wednesday.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 20-minute call if easier.

Best,
Alice

Attachment: novio_SIG-lite_request.pdf (1 page request form)

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@noviohealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Feb 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Novio procurement — subprocessor residency & CAIQ follow-up

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the note and the SIG-lite. I've attached our canonical subprocessor roster (CSV) and a short summary PDF that hits the three bullets you requested. High-level answers up front:

- We publish a current subprocessor roster and indicate residency per service. Most infra-facing subprocessors host in multi-region public cloud; we maintain onshore-only options for dedicted Private installs.
- Customer-managed KMS is supported for Redwood Private and Dedicated; hosted customers can opt for a customer KMS integration with envelope encryption for keys at rest.
- Ephemeral keys: the inference runtime issues short-lived session keys for model-serving worker processes; those keys are derived from a customer-scoped root while never exposing root key material to partners. Audit logs for ephemeral key issuance are retained per your SOC2 scope.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20260218.csv, sig-responses-summary-20260302.pdf

If you want, Karhtik (cc'd) can map the roster rows to the SIG questions directly and we can return a completed SIG-lite workbook by early next week. Let me know whether Novio needs an onshore-only commitment for production or just for backups/replicas.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0173

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@noviohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procure@noviohealth.com
Date: Thu, 27 Feb 2026 14:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Novio procurement — subprocessor residency & CAIQ follow-up

Hi Alice / Monica —

A couple quick clarifying items from the security team so our return is precise:

1) When you ask about "customer-managed KMS for hosted customers," do you need a HOLD on model artifacts or only on keys for customer data? Our hosted API supports envelope encryption with customer key wrapping but model weights remain managed by Redwood; for private deployments we can escrow model artifacts if required.

2) For "onshore-only" — is Novio asking for production inference traffic and data storage to be restricted to US regions, or is the requirement limited to long-term backups and audit logs? The implementation effort and timeline differ.

3) For the SIG-lite: would Novio accept a redline-first approach where we return the subprocessor/dataflow sections prefilled and highlight any questions that require legal/architectural sign-off? That speeds the procurement team time to review.

If you confirm 1+2, I'll assemble the SIG-lite responses and a short technical appendix that maps each subprocessor to the dataflow and KMS role.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Applied Security & Risk
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@noviohealth.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@noviohealth.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Novio procurement — subprocessor residency & CAIQ follow-up

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clarifications and for confirming timelines. Novio's ask for procurement (production residency in US and customer-managed KMS for all PII processing) is clear — we can meet this for a Dedicated or Private deployment.

Next steps we propose:
- Deliver completed SIG-lite subprocessor + dataflow sections (attached) by COB Thursday 2026-03-05.
- Provision a Temporary Onsite/Onshore plan document for Dedicated: timeline ~3–4 weeks for region pinning and KMS integration; we'll include milestone dates.
- Legal will draft the addendum to the SOW for the residency/KMS carve-out; expect a DocuSign link for signature once Novio confirms the SOW terms.

For transparency: the attached PDF lists the subprocessor roster rows referenced earlier, plus a short appendix on our ephemeral key lifecycle (Karthik authored). If Novio wants model-escrow language added to the SOW, escalate to legal now so we can include it in the DocuSign package.

DocuSign preview: https://app.docusign.com/preview/EXAMPLE-NVO-8342 (will become active once terms are final)

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0239

Attachments: sig-responses-summary-20260302.pdf, subprocessor_roster_20260218.csv
